title: Explainable anomaly signatures and contextual pager curation for SLO alerts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce noisy pages and improve on-call actionability by building explainable anomaly signatures that attach a compact, ranked context bundle to burn-rate and threshold alerts. This ticket implements: (1) lightweight tracing hooks to capture representative spans around anomalous latency/error events, (2) a metrics+logs fusion pipeline that emits normalized anomaly signatures, and (3) a pager curation layer that filters and annotates pages with a confidence score and suggested remediation steps. The goal is fewer low-value wakeups, faster root-cause triage, and measurable reduction in mean time to acknowledge for SLO breaches.
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly signature pipeline produces compact signature payloads (<= 2KB) for >= 95% of detected anomalies
Pager curation reduces duplicate pages for the same incident group by >= 40% in staging
Attached trace hooks include at least one representative span + request metadata for 90% of signatures
Dashboards show signal-level confidence and a breakdown of contributing signals (latency/5xx/queue-depth) for any fired SLO alert
Automated tests for signature generation and pager suppression rules with coverage threshold > 80%
steps: Design signature schema and storage TTL (Confluence: /display/OBS/Signature+Schema)
Add non-blocking tracing hooks in runtime request path and a sampler that favors anomalous buckets
Implement metrics/logs fusion job (Kafka->Beam->ClickHouse) to compute normalized signatures
Create pager curation service that deduplicates, ranks, and annotates pages before sending to PD
Wire Grafana dashboards and alert templates to include signature payload and remediation hints
Run staged experiment on dedicated capacity routes for 2 weeks and collect metrics
notes: Tradeoffs: storing richer trace context increases storage and privacy surface. We limit payloads to derived signature features and a single representative span; full traces remain accessible via link only.
Decision: prefer explainability over opaque ML scores for initial rollout. Confidence is a weighted rule-based score combining anomaly magnitude, tag density, and repeat rate.
Privacy: will redact customer PII; security review not required for this PR but will pass through privacy review checklist before prod rollout.
Operational concern: initial sampler may increase GPU-side tracing overhead by ~2-4% on p95; mitigation includes backpressure and adaptive sampling based on load
